# digna Documentation

> digna is a European AI-driven platform for Data Quality and Data Observability. It runs entirely inside the customer's own environment — on-premises or in a private cloud, never as SaaS — executing all data quality checks and anomaly detection directly inside the database engine, so data never leaves the customer's environment. digna has no access to customer data.

## Platform

- [Platform Overview](https://docs.digna.ai/platform/overview/): Technical overview of all digna modules — Data Anomalies, Data Analytics, Data Validation, Data Timeliness, and Data Schema Tracker.
- [Data Anomalies](https://docs.digna.ai/platform/data_anomalies/Introduction/): AI-based detection of irregularities in data volume, missing values, distributions, and column relationships — no manual rule writing required.
- [Data Analytics](https://docs.digna.ai/platform/data_analytics/Introduction/): Trend and volatility analysis for long-term data reliability, built on top of Data Anomalies metrics.
- [Data Validation](https://docs.digna.ai/platform/data_validation/Introduction/): Rule-based checks for deterministic, auditable data quality and compliance.
- [Data Timeliness](https://docs.digna.ai/platform/data_timeliness/Introduction/): Monitors on-time arrival of data deliveries and correlates delays with anomalies.
- [Data Schema Tracker](https://docs.digna.ai/platform/schema_tracker/Introduction/): Detects and tracks structural/schema changes in monitored datasets.

## Installation & Deployment

- [Windows Installation Guide (Release 2026.06)](<https://docs.digna.ai/installation_deployment/Windows/Release 2026.06/installation_guide_digna_windows_2026_06/>): System requirements, PostgreSQL setup, web server configuration (IIS/Tomcat), backend and dashboard configuration, running digna as a Windows service, upgrading.
- [Single Sign-On (SSO) Integration Guide](https://docs.digna.ai/installation_deployment/sso_integration_guide/): Configure OIDC-based SSO with Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta, and other OIDC-compliant identity providers.

## Database Integrations

digna connects to databases and warehouses via native drivers or ODBC. Setup guides:

- [PostgreSQL](https://docs.digna.ai/databases/postgres_connector_guide/)
- [Snowflake](https://docs.digna.ai/databases/snowflake_connector_guide/)
- [Databricks (Unity Catalog)](https://docs.digna.ai/databases/databricks_connector_guide/)
- [Databricks (Legacy)](https://docs.digna.ai/databases/databricks_legacy_connector_guide/)
- [Oracle](https://docs.digna.ai/databases/oracle_connector_guide/)
- [MS SQL Server](https://docs.digna.ai/databases/sqlserver_connector_guide/)
- [Teradata](https://docs.digna.ai/databases/teradata_connector_guide/)
- [Azure Synapse](https://docs.digna.ai/databases/azure_synapse_connector_guide/)
- [Apache Hive](https://docs.digna.ai/databases/hive_connector_guide/)
- [Netezza](https://docs.digna.ai/databases/netezza_connector_guide/)

## Notes

- This documentation is also available in 26 languages under a locale prefix, e.g. `/de/`, `/fr/`, `/ja/` (see the sitemap at https://docs.digna.ai/sitemap.xml for the full list). The URLs above are the canonical English versions.
